answer: Here is one mechanism that works: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because hollow only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, wharf is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any pigment approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
